digest.component_or_area: CI workflows and Git fetch optimization
propositions: CI workflows must apply --filter=blob:none to all tickets-store fetch operations to reduce transfer size and latency across checkout mechanisms (from 1.04 GiB/59s to 68.7 MiB/14.3s for standalone; from 6.73 minutes to sub-5-minute Gerrit verify-identity).

Named-remote filter inheritance and direct-URL explicit filters must both advertise Git protocol capability for filter support and preserve commit-graph integrity (no depth on full-history fetches; depth:1 retained on shallow Gerrit require-ticket).

Production guards must parse git count-objects pack size immediately after checkout/materialization and reject transfers exceeding REBAR_CHECKOUT_PACK_LIMIT_KIB=102400 (standalone) or REBAR_TICKETS_PACK_LIMIT_KIB=131072 (Gerrit post-materialization).

Real-Git test fixture must start git daemon with partial-clone support, capture packet traces for filter negotiation, verify missing-blob behavior before materialization, and prove size contrasts between filtered and unfiltered repos at configured thresholds.
Standalone verify-identity and Gerrit verify-identity scanning must leave exact git count-objects output unchanged after materialization, proving no promisor fetch leakage during identity operations.
Blobless filtered fetches plus worktree materialization must reconverge independent local/remote changes with ours driver, retain expected events, and successfully push merged commits.
